market_question: Will France send warships through the Strait of Hormuz by May 31, 2026?
reasoning: France maintains a permanent naval presence in the region via bases in Djibouti and the UAE, and routinely transits the Strait of Hormuz to access the Persian Gulf. The timeframe of over a year makes a transit nearly certain, and such movements are typically tracked by maritime spotters, defence analysts, and regional media, creating an 'overwhelming consensus of credible reporting' even if France doesn't issue a specific press release. The 4.5% market price severely underestimates this reality.
evidence_points: France contributes warships to the European-led EMASoH mission in the Strait of Hormuz area, ensuring regular transits.
Historical precedent: French frigates (e.g., Languedoc) transited Hormuz in 2023–2024, widely reported by naval tracking sources and press.
The resolution criteria accept 'overwhelming consensus of credible reporting', lowering the bar from an official French statement to well-documented sightings.
The long market window (through May 2026) makes at least one confirmed transit extremely probable.
sources_consulted: EMASoH mission updates (official and news reports)
MarineTraffic / AIS tracking discussions on social media and defence blogs
